newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bund futures tempted higher, hurdle at 101.00.
newsitem.headline: Bund futures tempted higher, hurdle at 101.00.

text.p: German Bunds and futures traded higher again early on Wednesday, adding to the impressive gains clocked up in the previous session on the back of lively U.S. Treasuries.
Traders said that while the positive mood -- sparked in the U.S. by a benign consumer price inflation data -- would continue to filter through, any gains this session were likely to be less dramatic.
Nevertheless, by 0643 GMT, the DTB June futures was 17 basis points higher on the day at 100.98, itching to tackle key resistance at 101.00.
The 101.00 level has not been seen by the June Bund contract since March 17, when the market broke sharply down from a high at 101.60 to close at 100.40.
In the cash market the benchmark 10-year Bund was staying close to home at 101.31 for a yield of 5.810 percent.

Analysts said the the Bundesbank's April report, released earlier, had confirmed a "balanced" German eocnomic scene and reinforced the market view that interest rates would remain stady for the time being.
"In all likelyhood, the evidence will remain mixed and the Bundesbank will stay unconcerned about prices," said one.
Charles Diebel, senior fixed income analyst at Technical Data in London said there was some impact on the market from talk of an estimated shortfall in German tax receipts for May.
"That is making people expect that even more restrictions on spending are going to be coming, which is all the more constructive for the debt market." he said.
But he said this session's activity was likely to be more subdued that on Tuesday.
"The reversal we had yesterday was quite dramatic. And it was partially sparked by a few stale shorts hanging around who started feeding on themselves."
"Now we're are almost a big figure higher than we were at this time yesterday, so some kind of pause and profit taking would seem likely," Diebel said.
Even so, the German cash market continued to outclass Treasuries, pushing the 10-year yield gap out to 118 basis points from around 116 at Tuesday's close.
Some analysts are predicting this spread could bloat to 120 basis points in the near term.
